beats.text: Give every human alive one square meter. How much land do we need?
Eight point two billion people. One square meter each, side by side.
Lock in your answer. Three. Two. One.
It sounds like a whole continent.
It's eight thousand two hundred square kilometers. That's Crete.
All of humanity fits on one Greek island, just barely.
Earth has eighteen thousand times more land than that.
Space isn't the problem. Food, water and energy are.

sources: World population mid-2026: about 8.2 billion (U.S. Census Bureau, International Database / World Population Day 2026; UN World Population Prospects 2024 gives a similar figure). 8.2 billion x 1 m2 = 8,200 km2.
Crete: 8,336 km2 (island area, Wikipedia 'Crete', geography section; the infobox gives 8,450 km2). Either way > 8,200 km2.
Earth's land area about 149 million km2 -> 149,000,000 / 8,200 = about 18,000.
Simplification: 1 m2 per person standing (not living space); outline from Natural Earth 1:110m (simplified).
